text:
maria: Heads-up — we hit fleet saturation in us-west-2 this morning. p95 latency spiked and several routes queued. Thinking about consolidating per-route queues into a small set of priority tiers to reduce fragmentation. anyone object?

jon: saw the alerts. p95 jumped to ~1.8s, route /gen-image qlen ~200. Per-route queues are leaving GPUs half-empty for some tenants while others pile up.

alex: +1 to consolidation but we should keep enterprise SLA routes isolated. propose hybrid: reserved queues for critical customers, shared priority pools for everything else.

sam: main risk is head-of-line blocking from large token-requests. we need admission controls that consider tokens-per-request, not just concurrency. size-based ordering could help.

maria: rough proposal: 3 tiers — realtime (SLA), regular, bulk. realtime gets strict per-request token cap + higher weight. regular is FIFO with aging. bulk is background-y and preemptable.

lee: agree on aging to avoid starvation. priority aging where regular->realtime over time if waiting too long. prevents permanent bulk starvation.

infra-bot: deploy-notification: canary config "admission_v2-hybrid" applied to us-west-2 by @deploy-bot at 1771504300 :information_source:

sam: quick config sketch to prototype (very rough):
```json
{
  "admission_mode": "hybrid",
  "tiers": ["realtime","regular","bulk"],
  "realtime": {
    "max_concurrent": 200,
    "max_tokens_per_request": 1024,
    "weight": 3
  },
  "aging_ms": 300000
}
```

jon: we should also include token-based admission and preemption. i.e. if cluster_util>0.9, start preempting bulk and throttle large token requests.

maria: cost angle — consolidation should improve GPU utilization (lower $/token) but tail latency for bulk jobs will increase, which is acceptable for most customers. want to quantify.

alex: i'll run an offline replay sim over 30 days of traces to estimate p50/p95 delta and utilization gain. need trace export: /infra/trace-export (link).

lee: another infra caveat: consolidation centralizes IO patterns. big batched workloads could saturate NICs on hosts. we should prototype per-host nic throttles and pod-level egress shaping.

ops-oncall: oncall here — if we flip this we need an emergency throttle and an alert when cluster headroom < 8% so we can revert quickly. add a playbook entry.

sam: rollout plan suggestion:
1) sim + offline replay (alex/sam)
2) canary 5% traffic with hybrid queues + aging
3) measure p50/p95, queued_wait_ms, preemptions, and cache cold-start impact
4) expand to 25% once metrics stable

maria: agree. owners: Alex+Sam = sim, Lee = NIC/shaping, Jon = admission runtime changes, Ops = dashboard & alerts. We'll put a formal RFC. Post updates to #eng-infra.

jon: metrics we must emit: queued_count_by_tier, avg_wait_ms_by_tier, preemptions, tokens_rejected, concurrent_by_tier. Also per-node nic_queue_depth.

alex: also capture per-customer latency buckets so we can guarantee enterprise SLA is preserved during canary.

maria: action items (short):
- sim results by EOD Wed
- canary config PR by Fri
- dashboard + alerts by Mon

lee: ack — I'll prototype k8s node annotations and tc-based shaping for NIC throttles (net-class annotation).

infra-bot: incident-bot: related incident 1771502100 — GPU saturation earlier today resolved by autoscale.

ops-oncall: i've added a rollback playbook: revert to per-route queues and disable preemption flags. include runbook steps.

maria: thanks everyone. please paste sim outputs and PR links here when ready. :thumbsup:
